## Observed on current main

At `0615405e35a3f42e82888e5f050afc642f2562d8` after [#283](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/pull/283), two of four [Deep jobs](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/actions/runs/43773461602) failed before dependency installation or any release test:

- [Node 22 / npm](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/actions/runs/43773461602/job/132994308657): npm exited 217, `ENOTEMPTY` renaming the existing npm installation, while its Node 22 sibling was in the same setup step.
- [Node 26 / Bun](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/actions/runs/43773461602/job/132994308731): `npm: command not found`, exit 127 at the global install command, just after its Node 26 sibling began replacing npm. The other two legs passed.

The [workflow at this commit](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ops/blob/0615405e35a3f42e82888e5f050afc642f2562d8/.github/workflows/ci-deep.yml#L20-L63) runs the four Node/launcher combinations in parallel. Each uses `npm install --global npm@11.21.0 --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` and checks the selected version before `npm ci`. Both failures occur during that step. The overlapping steps and symptoms are consistent with concurrent mutation of a common tool installation; filesystem topology and causation were not independently reproduced. This is a hosted CI setup defect, not a failing package behavior or publish result.

## Expected result and regression coverage

- Each job uses npm 11.21.0 throughout setup and the gates without replacing a shared global executable or mutating a sibling's toolchain. Keep the pin and exact-version assertion.
- Exercise two overlapping launcher jobs per Node version in a disposable same-host or shared-cache fixture, from both cold and warm states. Assert both tools stay available and correctly pinned, both jobs reach clean dependency install, and the original four Deep gates still run.
- Keep the hosted fallback, distinct gates, and existing protection/coverage unchanged. Show that all four exact-head Deep jobs pass on the fix; a serial run alone does not exercise the observed overlap.

No runner, shared installation, workflow, or provider was changed to gather this evidence.
